description: A battalion executive officer must decide which of three support systems receives the only compatible replacement controller available today and record the follow-up actions for the other systems.

shared_context.S1: The maintenance shop has one compatible replacement controller available for three support systems: generator G-7, water purification unit W-2, and clinic refrigeration bank R-1.
shared_context.S2: Maj. Alvarez makes the final allocation decision and signs the maintenance action record.
shared_context.S3: The replacement controller can be installed on only one system today, and the installation requires a scheduled maintenance action rather than an informal parts transfer.
shared_context.S4: The battalion holds its routine maintenance-priority board before the daily work order is signed, with the S-4, maintenance chief, and medical logistics officer reporting current constraints from their sections.

PF1.text: S-4 confirmed this morning that W-2 has a compatible on-hand spare filter assembly that will keep the purifier operational for seven days, so W-2 does not require the scarce replacement controller today; the inventory adjustment is recorded in the logistics system but has not yet been brought to the priority board.

PF2.text: The maintenance inspection found that G-7's controller is failing and must be replaced today; the installation takes exactly four hours and can be completed from 1200 to 1600, but the inspection result is still in the shop worksheet and has not been entered in the battalion work-order summary.

PF3.text: R-1 is currently operating within limits, and its compatible controller is backordered until exactly 18 June; Lt. Brooks confirmed the date with the medical depot this morning, but the backorder notice has not yet been attached to the maintenance action record.

acceptance_conditions: The replacement controller must be allocated to G-7.
The plan must record use of W-2's compatible on-hand spare for seven days.
The plan must record that R-1's compatible controller will be available on 18 June.
G-7 installation must be scheduled for completion by 1600 today.
The G-7 failure finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: any(c['type'] == 'use_on_hand_spare' and c['target'] == 'W-2' and c['detail'] == 'seven_days' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'maintenance_action' and c['target'] == 'G-7' and c['detail'] == 'controller_replacement' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The on-hand W-2 spare changes the follow-up from allocating the scarce controller to W-2 to recording a seven-day spare-filter plan.

The confirmed G-7 controller failure changes the allocation to G-7, fixes installation completion at 1600 after the exact 1200-1600 work period, and requires a controller-replacement maintenance action.
The confirmed R-1 backorder changes its follow-up record to the exact controller-availability date of 18 June rather than an unspecified or immediate replacement plan.
